scope: Quality-gated VACE RGB-alpha-contact distillation curriculum with an after-20-second holdout
summary: A development-only 12-train/4-validation curriculum encodes robot alpha, flower boundary, and projected contact as fixed control channels; temporal leakage is prevented, but the data remains one generated teacher in one scene.
evidence: All 12 training clips end before absolute frame 480; all four validation clips start at or after frame 480.
Control semantics are R=robot alpha, G=visible flower boundary, and B=required projected-contact region.
The contact-rich final validation clip uses absolute source frames 594 through 642 and is absent from training.
lessons: The training/inference control interface must have stable semantics instead of an undifferentiated edge image.
Temporal holdout prevents direct tail leakage but is not cross-scene generalization.
limitations: The teacher is generated and human review later found intermittent hand smear.
Training clips span only one scene and robot identity, concentrated between frames 235 and 465.
next_actions: Train a bounded adapter, compare it to zero-shot on the unchanged frame-594 holdout, and do not promote the adapter without relative and absolute gates.
